sections.name: What Is RCM
sections.heading: The work between a patient booking and your practice collecting payment.
sections.intro: Revenue cycle management connects patient information, coverage review, charges, claims, payments and follow-up. Each stage depends on what happened before it and what the next person needs to know. A useful workflow keeps those handoffs clear.
sections.body: A coverage question before a visit can become a billing question later. Clear handoffs help your team understand what happened, what information is missing and who needs to act next.

cards.title: Before the visit
cards.body: Prepare patient and insurance information. Identify eligibility and authorization questions that need review.

cards.title: During the visit
cards.body: Keep the documented service, charge information and billing requirements aligned with the practice’s process.

cards.title: After the visit
cards.body: Follow claim status, unresolved denials, payments and outstanding balances through the next review step.

sections.name: Services Pipeline
sections.heading: Follow the work from registration to payment.
sections.intro: The revenue cycle runs through eight connected stages. This diagram maps the cycle; confirm which stages, connections and actions ConvergeFlow supports for your practice during the demo.

pipeline.title: Patient Registration
pipeline.body: Start with the patient, appointment and insurance information your team needs for the visit.

pipeline.title: Eligibility Verification
pipeline.body: Review coverage information and keep incomplete or unclear responses visible before the appointment.

pipeline.title: Prior Authorization
pipeline.body: Identify authorization questions, supporting information and the status that needs follow-up.

pipeline.title: Charge Capture and Coding
pipeline.body: Connect the services documented with the coding and charge details needed for billing review.

pipeline.title: Claims Submission
pipeline.body: Review claim readiness, submission status and items that need correction or another look.

pipeline.title: Denial Management
pipeline.body: Keep denial reasons, review responsibilities and follow-up actions connected to the account.

pipeline.title: Payment Posting
pipeline.body: Review remittance and payment information alongside the balance and any outstanding questions.

pipeline.title: AR and Reporting
pipeline.body: See outstanding balances and aging, and decide which follow-up work needs attention.

cards.title: Prepare the visit
cards.body: Patient information, eligibility review and authorization questions set the context for the work ahead.

cards.title: Prepare the claim
cards.body: Charge and coding information need to support the billing review and submission process.

cards.title: Work the exceptions
cards.body: Rejected, incomplete or denied items need a clear reason, an owner and a next action.

cards.title: Follow the balance
cards.body: Review payments, receivables and aging with the account context needed for follow-up.

sections.name: Industries
sections.heading: Start with the way your team works.
sections.intro: Start with your appointment schedule, payer questions and billing handoffs. Choose your practice type to focus the product discussion on the work your team handles.

cards.title: Dental Practices
cards.body: Review appointments, insurance context and eligibility questions in the dental workflow.

cards.title: DSO and Group Practices
cards.body: Discuss practice-level visibility, consistent review steps and oversight across locations.

cards.title: Medical Clinics
cards.body: Review your specialty, payer and system requirements before confirming medical-specific fit.

cards.title: Specialty Practices
cards.body: Define the service-specific information and follow-up questions your team needs to handle.

cards.title: Hospitals and Health Systems
cards.body: Discuss organizational scope, system boundaries and the review requirements for an enterprise evaluation.

cards.title: Behavioral Health
cards.body: Bring your appointment, coverage and billing workflow requirements to a focused fit discussion.

cards.title: RCM Billing Companies
cards.body: Discuss how client context, work ownership and reporting should connect across the accounts you review.

sections.name: How It Works
sections.heading: Start with your systems and the work your team handles.
sections.intro: Start with the work your team needs to understand, then confirm the systems, information and available capabilities required to support it.

steps.title: Map the practice systems
steps.body: Identify where appointments, patient information and billing records are held. Confirm the systems and data flows relevant to your evaluation.

steps.title: Define the payer workflow
steps.body: List the coverage and authorization questions, required information and follow-up responsibilities for your practice.

steps.title: Review the available product views
steps.body: Walk through verification, eligibility, claims and receivables screens. Ask what can be configured and what requires confirmation.

steps.title: Agree how exceptions are handled
steps.body: Determine who reviews incomplete information and how the next step is communicated. Keep questions open until the workflow is understood.

steps.title: Set the measures for follow-up
steps.body: Choose the reporting scope and baseline your team needs to judge the workflow after an implementation decision.

sections.name: Technology
sections.heading: How information moves through the workflow.
sections.intro: Bring your PMS or EHR name, payer requirements and access questions to the demo. Use these areas to discuss supported connections, technical boundaries and responsibility for the next action.

cards.title: Portal Workflows
cards.body: Confirm which payer workflows are available, what information is retrieved and how unresolved portal work is reviewed.

cards.title: API and Clearinghouse Connectivity
cards.body: Ask which interfaces are supported and what the available transactions return for your requirements.

cards.title: Credential Management
cards.body: Discuss access, credential handling and the evidence your organization needs before connecting any systems.

cards.title: Workflow Orchestration
cards.body: Review scheduling, routing, retries and human review responsibilities across the available workflow.

cards.title: Exception Handling
cards.body: Inspect how incomplete or failed work is represented and how the next review action is identified.

cards.title: Reporting and Activity Visibility
cards.body: Confirm report fields, activity scope and the information your team can inspect during review.

sections.name: Results and Measurement
sections.heading: Choose what your team needs to measure.
sections.intro: Start with a baseline your team understands. Keep the scope, dates and definitions consistent so a later comparison reflects the work you intended to review.

cards.title: Review workload
cards.body: Track the work entering the queue and the items still waiting for attention.

cards.title: Claim follow-up
cards.body: Review corrections and denials with the context and ownership needed to investigate them.

cards.title: Payment visibility
cards.body: Compare payment and balance views within a consistent reporting scope.

cards.title: Outstanding receivables
cards.body: Look at aging and follow-up work over a defined review period.

sections.name: Product Walkthrough — Customer Evidence Slot
sections.heading: See the product against a familiar practice scenario.
sections.intro: Ask to see an appointment queue item, an eligibility flag and a receivables view. Follow the information your team needs and identify the questions still open.

cards.title: Before the visit
cards.body: What should your team see when an appointment has an unresolved coverage question?

cards.title: Across the claim
cards.body: What context does the next person need when an item requires correction or follow-up?

cards.title: At the practice review
cards.body: Which report or activity record would help your team understand the outstanding work?
